title: Classifying x^2 + x: Neither Symmetry
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Show that f(x)=x^2+x is neither even nor odd.

steps.title: Compute f(-x)
steps.explanation: Squaring keeps the first term, but the linear term changes sign.
steps.why: Mixed parities of exponents behave differently under negation.

steps.title: Test the Even Condition
steps.explanation: For any nonzero x the expressions differ, e.g. f(1)=2 while f(-1)=0, so f is not even.
steps.why: A single counterexample disproves the identity f(-x)=f(x).

steps.title: Test the Odd Condition
steps.explanation: The right side is -x^2-x, whose leading sign pattern differs from x^2-x; again f(1)=2 while -f(-1)=0. So f is not odd.
steps.why: Oddness would require every output to flip sign, which fails at x=1.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.explanation: Both symmetry tests fail, so the parabola-like graph has no y-axis or origin symmetry.
steps.why: A polynomial is even iff all powers are even and odd iff all powers are odd; x^2+x has both types.
